answer: The nebula multiplier is published, charged in nadir, and ocean lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 9 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 523 identities would post 3189 proofs and burn roughly 79 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
